sources.title: Source systems
sources.description: Systems whose record IDs are kept as external references. A source is never deleted: deactivate it to stop new references and imports.
sources.emptyHint: Add the systems you import or synchronise records from.
sources.codeHint: Lower-case letters, digits, - and _ (e.g. salesforce). Used in import files and API URLs; cannot be changed later.

errors.unknownType: This record type cannot have external references.
errors.externalIdRequired: Give the external ID with the source system.
errors.externalIdTooLong: The external ID is too long (255 characters at most).
errors.externalIdTaken: This external ID is already linked to another record.
errors.recordAlreadyReferenced: This record already has another external ID from this source.
errors.duplicateExternalId: The same external ID appears twice in the file.
errors.keyMismatch: The external ID points at another record than this row.
errors.codeFormat: Use lower-case letters, digits, - and _ (2–50 characters).
errors.codeTaken: A source system with this code already exists.
errors.ipRefused: Calls from this address are not allowed for this client.
errors.rateLimited: Too many requests for this client; try again in a minute.
errors.clientOnly: Only integration clients can read the feeds and extracts.
errors.recordTypeOutsideSystems: Choose record types of the allowed systems only.
errors.ipEntry: Give one address or CIDR block per line (at most 50).
errors.expiry: Choose an expiry date in the future, at most {{max}} days from today.
errors.webhookEvent: Choose events of the client's allowed systems.
errors.cursor: The cursor is not valid; start again without it.
errors.exportRootMissing: The operator has not set an export directory (Integration:ExportRoot).
errors.exportFolder: Give a folder inside the export directory (no absolute paths and no "..").

clients.title: Integration clients
clients.description: Named service accounts of other systems. Each client reads only its allowed systems, within the data scope of its roles and acting unit. A person's personal access token is not used for system integrations.
clients.emptyHint: Create a client for Power BI, a data warehouse or another system that reads this one.
clients.name: Client
clients.kindHint: API key for BI tools (Power BI, Excel) and simple scripts; OAuth 2.0 client credentials for systems that support it.
clients.recordTypesHint: Tick record types to limit the client to them; none ticked means every record type of the system.
clients.allRecordTypes: Every record type of the allowed systems
clients.actingUnitHint: Unit and unit-and-below data scopes of the client's roles apply to this unit.

scopeNames.feeds: Analytics feeds and extracts (OData, changed / deleted)

clients.ipHint: One address or CIDR block per line (e.g. 10.20.30.0/24). Empty: any address.
clients.expiresHint: Empty: the default lifetime from Settings → Integrations.
clients.secretOnce: Copy the secret now: it is shown only once and cannot be read again.
clients.howApiKey: Send it as "Authorization: Bearer <key>", or in Power BI / Excel choose Basic with the client ID as user name and the key as password.
clients.howOAuth: Request a token at /connect/token with grant_type=client_credentials and scope=feeds, then call the feeds with "Authorization: Bearer <token>".
clients.revokeWarning: The client stops working at once and for good: its credentials and tokens are refused and its webhooks stop. Create a new client to reconnect.
clients.permissionsHint: The client holds these roles like a user: their permissions and data scopes (own, team, unit, unit and below, all) decide what it reads. Only roles of the allowed systems are offered.
clients.noRoles: No roles in the allowed systems.
clients.overlapHint: 0 ends them at once; up to 30 days lets the other system switch over.
clients.oauthRotateHint: OAuth: the new secret replaces the current one at once.
clients.revokeCredentialWarning: Calls with this credential are refused from now on.

webhooks.hint: Signed HTTP POSTs to the other system when events happen in records this client may read.
webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.urlHint: HTTPS. Addresses on this server, link-local and cloud metadata addresses are refused.
webhooks.testQueued: Test event queued; it is sent within a minute.
webhooks.verifyHint: Receivers check X-Strategy-Signature = v1=HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<X-Strategy-Timestamp>.<body>") and refuse timestamps older than 5 minutes.

deliveries.title: Webhook deliveries
deliveries.description: Every webhook delivery with its attempts. Failed deliveries are retried with exponential back-off and then move to the dead-letter list; replay sends them again.

exports.hint: Writes the records changed since the last run to a folder under the server's export directory, as this client (its scope). SFTP and S3: sync that folder or pull the extract API.
exports.name: Name
exports.folderHint: A sub-folder of the export directory set by the operator (e.g. power-bi/nightly).

portal.title: Developer portal
portal.description: How other systems read this one: REST API, OData analytics feeds, incremental extracts and webhooks. Feeds are read by integration clients only.
portal.feedsIntro: One read-only OData v4 service per system. The metadata below is what a client with your permissions would see.
portal.noSystems: You cannot read any system that has feeds.

query.select: $select, $filter (eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, and, or, not, in, contains, startswith, endswith), $orderby, $top, $skip, $count.
query.filter: Filter on codes and values, not on the …Label display properties.
query.expand: $expand follows the relationships of a record type, with $select, $filter, $orderby and $top inside.
query.paging: Large results come in pages: follow @odata.nextLink.
query.labels: Codes are always included; …Label properties give the label in the language of the lang parameter (ar or en).
query.scope: Every row and every expanded row is filtered by the client's permissions and data scope.

portal.extractsIntro: For ETL tools: records changed since a time, and a feed of deleted (cancelled / inactive) records, in JSON or CSV.

extracts.cursor: Pages are ordered by modification time; pass nextCursor back while hasMore is true.
extracts.watermark: Store watermark and send it as changedSince on the next run.
extracts.deleted: Records are never removed: cancelled, withdrawn and inactive records appear in the deleted feed.
extracts.csv: format=csv returns UTF-8 CSV with code and label columns; the cursor and watermark come in X-Next-Cursor / X-Watermark headers.

portal.webhooksIntro: Events a client can subscribe to. Payloads carry the ids, codes and changed values; read the record through the feeds for the rest.
portal.signatureHeaders: Headers: X-Strategy-Event, X-Strategy-Delivery (deduplicate on it), X-Strategy-Timestamp, X-Strategy-Signature.
portal.signatureRetry: Answer 2xx within 10 seconds. Other answers are retried with exponential back-off (8 attempts), then the delivery goes to the dead-letter list.

powerbi.intro: Power BI Desktop reads the feeds with its OData connector. Ask an administrator for an integration client (API key) with the systems and roles you need.

steps.1: In Power BI Desktop choose Get data → OData feed.
steps.2: Paste the feed URL of the system, e.g. {{url}}, and choose OK.
steps.3: When asked for credentials choose Basic: user name = the client ID (ic_…), password = the API key (sik_…). Choose the feed URL level so every system of this server uses them.
steps.4: In the navigator tick the entity sets you need (e.g. Projects, Milestones) and choose Load or Transform data.
steps.5: For Arabic labels add ?lang=ar to the URL; codes stay the same so relationships and measures keep working.
steps.6: To refresh in the Power BI service, publish the report and set the same Basic credentials in the dataset's data source settings (an on-premises data gateway is needed when this server is not reachable from the internet).
steps.7: If refreshes start failing with 401, the key was rotated, expired or the client was revoked; with 429 lower the refresh frequency or ask for a higher rate limit.

powerbi.other: Excel (Data → From OData feed), Tableau (OData connector) and Qlik (OData / REST connector) use the same URL and Basic credentials.

portal.apiIntro: The REST API is described by its OpenAPI document. Integration clients with the "Read the REST API" access can call GET endpoints with the same permissions.

auth.basic: Basic: client ID as user name and the API key as password (BI tools).
auth.oauth: OAuth 2.0 client credentials: POST /connect/token (grant_type=client_credentials, scope=feeds or api.read).
auth.limits: Calls outside the IP allow-list get 403; above the rate limit 429 with Retry-After; expired or revoked clients 401.

sync.title: Salesforce sync
sync.description: One-way standby copy of Salesforce: records, people, files and approval history are read from Salesforce and kept here read-only, so this system can take over when Salesforce is unavailable. Nothing is ever written to Salesforce.
sync.noConnectionHint: The connection is created when the application starts; restart the application or check the logs.

status.disabledHint: Fill in the connection, store the private key, test the connection, then activate the sync.
status.fullLoadWarning: A full load reads every record of every enabled object again (Bulk API). Records whose values did not change are skipped. It can take a long time and uses API capacity.
status.deactivateWarning: Scheduled runs stop and records are no longer read-only. Synced data stays.

connection.title: Connection
connection.loginUrlHint: https://login.salesforce.com, https://test.salesforce.com or your My Domain URL (HTTPS).
connection.clientIdHint: Consumer key of the Connected App that uses the JWT bearer flow.
connection.usernameHint: Salesforce user name of the read-only integration user.
connection.bulkThresholdHint: Objects with more changed records than this are read with Bulk API 2.0.
connection.keyHint: The private key of the Connected App's certificate signs the sign-in (JWT). It is stored encrypted and is never shown again.
connection.pemHint: Paste the key or choose the .pem / .key file. Storing a new key replaces the old one.

schedule.businessHoursHint: A run that falls outside business hours moves to the next business-hours start.
schedule.lateAfterHint: Administrators are told when no run succeeded for this long. Empty: twice the interval.
schedule.noRuns: No run is planned (the sync is not in standby).
schedule.previewHint: Planned times of the saved schedule.

mappings.hint: Objects are read in this order. An object can be enabled only after its mapping was validated against the live Salesforce describe.
mappings.noPack: Choose a mapping pack on the Connection tab
mappings.importInvalid: The file is not a mapping pack (JSON).

editor.title: Mapping of {{object}}
editor.description: Salesforce fields on one side, the fields of this system on the other.
editor.saveClears: Saving any change clears the validation: validate again before the object can be enabled.
editor.externalIdHint: {Id} by default; e.g. {Id}-{year:End_Date__c} for one record per year.
editor.whereHint: Optional, e.g. IsActive = true. No semicolons or sub-queries.
editor.useBulk: Use Bulk API for large loads
editor.defaultsHint: Target field → value used when Salesforce leaves it empty.
editor.ignoreHint: One per line: fields deliberately not mapped (the validator does not list them).
editor.optionsHint: People matching or history options; leave empty for records.
editor.invalidJson: Defaults and options must be valid JSON.
editor.saved: The mapping is saved; validate it again
editor.valid: The mapping is valid and confirmed
editor.validHint: The object can now be enabled.
editor.describeFailed: The Salesforce describe could not be read

transforms.yesNo: Yes / No / TBD → yes / no / empty

exceptionsTab.mapValueHint: Added to the field's value map, then the record is re-processed.
exceptionsTab.stillOpen: The record still has an exception

mode.standby: Salesforce is primary; this system is the standby copy
mode.primary: This system is primary — Salesforce is not being synced
mode.reconciling: Back in standby — reconciling the outage

failover.explain: When Salesforce is unavailable, make this system primary: records unlock, approvals, jobs and notifications resume here. Afterwards, re-enter the changes in Salesforce with the outage changes report and return to standby.
failover.makePrimaryWarning: Scheduled syncs stop and every synced record becomes editable here. Records with a pending Salesforce approval must be resubmitted here. This is recorded in the audit trail with your reason.
failover.codeSent: A code was sent to your e-mail address.
failover.noMfa: Set up two-step verification (authenticator app or e-mail) in your profile before making this system primary.

banner.primary: Salesforce outage: this system is primary

outage.title: Outage
outage.ackCheckbox: I have exported or reviewed the outage changes report
outage.returnWarning: Records become read-only again and the sync resumes. Salesforce versions of records changed here wait for your decision (Keep local / Take Salesforce).
outage.closeWarning: From now on Salesforce wins again for every record. Re-entered marks and the report stay available.

report.title: Outage changes report
report.hint: Every change made here during the outage, by system and record, to re-enter in Salesforce. Exporting acknowledges the report.
report.empty: No changes were made here during the outage.
report.truncated: The report is truncated; export it for the complete list.
report.exportFailed: The report could not be exported

conflicts.title: Conflicts
conflicts.hint: Salesforce sent a newer version of these records, which were changed here during the outage.

badges.readOnlyHint: {{source}} is the primary system: change this record in {{source}}; the change arrives here with the next sync.
badges.resubmitHint: The approval of this record was pending in Salesforce when this system became primary: submit it again here.

history.title: History from {{source}}
history.hint: Read-only: approval steps and field changes as recorded in the source system.

errors.readOnly: This record is synced from {{source}} and is read-only while {{source}} is the primary system. Make the change in {{source}}.
errors.apiLimit: The Salesforce API limit is almost used up; the run stopped and continues with the next run.
errors.apiVersion: Give the API version as v and a number, e.g. v62.0.
errors.authFailed: Salesforce refused the sign-in: check the consumer key, the integration user, the certificate and that the user is pre-authorised for the External Client App (or Connected App).
errors.bulkFailed: A Salesforce Bulk API query failed.
errors.conflictsPending: {{count}} conflicts still wait for a decision.
errors.duplicateKey: Two objects of the pack have the same key.
errors.everyHours: Give a number of hours from 1 to 24.
errors.externalIdTemplate: The external ID template must contain {Id}.
errors.invalidField: This Salesforce field name is not valid.
errors.invalidKey: The private key is not a valid PEM RSA key.
errors.invalidObject: This Salesforce object does not exist or the integration user cannot read it.
errors.loginUrl: Give an HTTPS Salesforce login URL that the outbound address policy allows.
errors.modeTransition: This action is not possible in the current mode ({{mode}}).
errors.notConfigured: The connection is not complete: login URL, consumer key, integration user and private key are needed.
errors.notConfirmed: Validate the mapping against Salesforce before enabling the object.
errors.notReady: Test the connection successfully before activating the sync.
errors.notStandby: The sync runs only in standby.
errors.packFormat: The file is not a mapping pack of a supported format.
errors.reportNotAcknowledged: Export or acknowledge the outage changes report first.
errors.scheduleKind: Choose every N hours, daily or weekly.
errors.where: The filter is not allowed (no semicolons or sub-queries).
